title.narrative: CO-National Convening on JET in Cambodia

description.narrative:
Cambodia is one among most vulnerable countries to climate change and impact of climate change, necessitating attention the need toprevent and mitigate impacts of climate on the country, especially on marginalized communities and social groups. Noticeably, Cambodia is undergoing a very rapid economic transformation, and this is leading to a growing demand for energy. While the benefits of this economic development are undoubted, there is a danger that Cambodia is on an unsustainable trajectory, both economically and environmentally. The Ministry of Mines and Energy (MME) acknowledges the urgency of meeting energy demand in an affordable, reliable, and secure manner, while adhering to national and global commitments on the climate and environment, maximizing the deployment of domestic renewable energy resources and energy efficiency measures, and excluding the development of additional coal plants and hydropower plants on the mainstream Mekong River. As Cambodia transits away from non-renewable and looks to scale up renewable energy sources like solar, wind and pumped storage hydropower, a Just Energy Transition (JET) is crucial to ensure that the shift is human-centred, equitable and “leaves no one behind”. This means that the benefits and costs of thetransition are distributed fairly and equitably, not negatively impacting vulnerable populations such as low-income families, minority communities, and workers in high-carbon industries. Recognizing the significance of JET within Cambodia's development context, Oxfam acknowledges it as a critical priority. While the government has made efforts to promote a clean energy transition in the country, the collaborative involvement of various stakeholders, including CSOs, the private sector, communities, academia, and researchers, is essential to ensure a just, fast, and inclusive transition. Their collective engagement plays a crucial role in shaping Cambodia's future energy landscape. To facilitate andencourage the engagement and involvement, the National Convening on JET in Cambodia is organized as a safe and inclusive platform.
The primary objective of the national convening on JET in Cambodia is to foster dialogue and propose an engagement statement at thenational level, emphasizing the importance ofJET within the ASEAN agenda during the ASEAN 2024 Chairmanship. The outcomes and conclusions drawn from the national convening will subsequently be shared and integrated into the regional convening scheduled for August2024. The specific objectives of the workshop include: • Increase understanding among participants on the overview of the energy landscape in Cambodia, encompassing achievements, challenges, and plans. • Establish a platform for meaningful discussions among key stakeholders regarding theJET landscape in Cambodia, focusing on its status, issues, and potential solutions. • Generate key statements and proposed recommendations to promote JET within Cambodia and advocate for its inclusion in the ASEAN agenda during the ASEAN 2024 Chairmanship.
The National Convening on JET in Cambodia will bring together various stakeholders, including representatives from CSOs, private sectors, communities, academia, and researchers. Their active participation is crucial in shaping and guiding the energy transition process and policy framework to ensure it is fair, fast, and inclusive. It is anticipated that around 60 participants will attend this significant event, contributing their diverse perspectives and expertise to drive meaningful change in Cambodia'senergy landscape toward just transition.

participating-org.narrative: Oxfam Novib is one of the 17 national affiliates of the Oxfam International Confederation. It started life in 1956 as the Netherlands Organisation for International Assistance (Novib), and joined forces with Oxfam in 1994. Working together in confederation, the Oxfam affiliates can speak with one clear and compelling voice on issues of global concern: climate change, health and education forall, agriculture, trade, and conflicts and emergencies. Oxfam established this country office to support local organizations and projects. Through this local office Oxfam Novib directly contributes towards this project#s implementation.
